Inonu-Wigner contractions of flag manifolds
Now describe construction of Inonu-Wigner contraction of a flag manifold G/H.

Let ∆ be corresponding Newton polytope and Γ ⊂ ∆ is some proper face of it. As it was already mentioned, the face Γ can be defined by the normal vector f ∈ R n with integer coefficients. In its turn, this vector f defines the filtration of the Lie algebra g by the following way
F a g = h ⊕   f (j)≤a m j   , a ∈ Z.(55)
As usual we can now take the graded Lie algebra g f corresponding to this filtration as follows
g Γ = a∈Z g (a) Γ , where g (a) Γ = F a g/ b<a F b g.(56)

Note that we have the inclusion h ⊂ g Γ , so there exists the Lie group G Γ with Lie algebra g Γ and the subgroup H ⊂ G Γ . Therefore, we can consider the homogeneous manifold M Γ = G Γ /H which is called Inonu-Wigner contraction of manifold M by the face Γ ⊂ ∆.
It is important that Newton polytope of the contraction M Γ is very face Γ and, moreover, its scalar curvature is truncation of the scalar curvature of M on the face Γ.

The same can be said also for corresponding Einstein equations. Also it is easy to see that Einstein metrics on M Γ have vanishing scalar curvature and all its derivatives, so the Ricci tensor vanish. Consequently, Einstein metrics on the contraction M Γ are Ricci-flat, so we have the following theorem.

It is important that some faces can be deleted from consideration due to their geometric properties because corresponding discriminant conditions necessarily hold. For example, it is obvious that for any vertex v we have that t −v s v (t) is non-zero constant, so discriminant condition holds. Further, generalization of vertex is n-dimensional face Γ = Conv(v ∪ Γ ) such that all vertices except one belong to (n − 1)-dimensional subface Γ ⊂ Γ. We call such faces pyramidal and we have the following lemma for them.Other type of face that we call octahedral for which discriminant conditions almostalways hold is defined by the following way. It is a convex hull of the points c + z i , c − z i , where z i , i = 1, ..., n are arbitrary linear independent vectors in R d , and c ∈ R d is some vector called center of octahedral face. For these faces we have the lemma. Let Γ be octahedral face with center −e i 0 such that all other points −e i , i = i 0 don't belong to Γ. Then corresponding discriminant condition holds if and only if [m i 0 , m i 0 ] = 0.Discriminant conditions for all other faces of Newton polytope ∆ need to be checked separately every time. Therefore, we are mostly interested in faces that are not pyramidal and not octahedral. We will call such faces marked.
